template.name: germinate
template.means: Walks every aspect of a situation as seeds and grows the path to the goal as a tree: roots the problem, trunk the ordered effort, branches the resources it leans on, limits what is out of reach, locks what no step may bend, fruit the state that ends the work. Closes on an assumption that can be knocked down in one line.

iterate.user-input: the emitted format is being replaced by glyph-package, and the parser discards the operator that the new format exists to record

problem.user-input: the emitted format is being replaced by glyph-package, and the parser discards the operator that the new format exists to record

instruction.user-input: carry the operator from the lexer to the XML, derive the golden from the specification, rederive the vectors, gate before emitter, decide the inverse, rewrite the reference, republish the skill

reference.user-input: the five examples, pure glyph plus verified engine output
BUNDLE_TARGET.md, the specification for the six layers
XML_REFERENCE.md lines 99 to 101, where extend, comma and divide are documented
chainElement in glyph-parser.js, the marker the engine computes and never serialises

restriction.user-input: out of scope: the six-layer bundle emitters, the agent file writer, the _ORBITAL runtime, the RAG retrieval engine

constraint.user-input: the operator reaches the XML before any chain element is emitted, and the golden derives from the specification, never from an implementation

never.user-input: no self-attested gate, and no acceptance criterion rewritten so the work passes

target.user-input: a compiler whose emitted format records the operator it was given, and whose inverse returns what went in

ready.user-input: each fruit stated as an observable condition, not as an intention

assumption.user-input: the language sweep rides in this release, because the vectors, the reference and both skills are already being rewritten

question.user-input: knock this down in one line and the tree becomes a new version

validate.user-input: the four guarantees the current XML makes: editorial force, block segmentation, needs, and exact string fidelity
